account: Today appears ordinary so far; I have no direct evidence of a hidden gathering or project. During my morning market walk, several townsfolk repeated that the baker had carried wheat at the bakery. The neighbour likewise said the baker was preparing fresh bread for today's market and that the east-bank quarter seemed quiet. This is consistent with ordinary baking, not evidence of anything unusual. The neighbour confirmed our usual three o'clock tea at their east-bank dockside cottage, though I still do not know the precise cottage. The secretary has been checking those arrangements. One discrepancy worth remembering: the secretary initially said the appointments chest was empty, although I had read the book there and saw the secretary take it out. Later the secretary said both days' appointments were safely returned. That could simply reflect handling the book; I cannot infer deception. I have kept my market walk and lunch engagements and am now at town hall for thirteen o'clock accounts. I have asked the secretary about income, expenses, requests, and the tea address, and am awaiting a reply. My feeling that something is happening without me remains a suspicion, not an established fact; I do not yet know who would be involved or what its purpose would be.
